The EU will ban social networks for under 13 and personal accounts for under 15

Ursula von der Leyen announced the framework of the future EU Kids Act in Strasbourg on September 16 in a speech about the state of the Union. The formal text will be presented by the Commission on Thursday together with Henna Virkkunen, Vice President for Technological Sovereignty.

The scheme is strict and gradual.
Under 13 years old, social networks are off-limits.
From 13 to 15, only "mini-accounts" are allowed: created and managed by parents, with limited features and time restrictions.

From 15 to 18, teenagers can create their own profile, but the platform must maintain a safe design: without addictive features, with enhanced settings.

Von der Leyen summarized it succinctly: "No social networks until 13. No personal account until 15." And separately: "Each age group has its own vulnerability. Therefore, each will have its own level of protection."

The essence of the law is not in another clause in the user agreement. Currently, a child can simply enter a fake birthdate and proceed. The Kids Act should make age verification a mandated obligation, not just a declaration. Brussels looked at Australia, which was the first to introduce a lower limit.
The logic of responsibility is also changing. "Platforms must prove that they are safe," said von der Leyen. "It's not about minors accessing social networks. It's about when and how we allow social networks to reach minors."

In the same speech, she listed what Europe is "not obliged to accept": features tailored to induce dependence; feeds that draw users into increasingly harsh content; photos of girls that AI turns into sexualized images. According to her, children in the EU spend four to six hours a day on screens. She called this "the capture of attention, focus, and consciousness" and "the theft of childhood."

Drafts that agencies saw before the speech go beyond social networks. Video platforms, online games, and AI chatbots could also fall under the same age ladder. The project discusses penalties for violators of up to 6% of global revenue. Until 18 years old, they want to remove autoplay, rewards for reposts, personal recommendations, and free messages from strangers on children's accounts.

This is not yet law. The text will go to the European Parliament and to the 27 capitals. France pushed for a minimum age of 15, Spain spoke of 16, the Commission's expert panel leaned towards 13. The compromise announced today falls right in the middle: complete shield until 13, a parental corridor until 15, "safe design" until adulthood.

If the text passes close to what was announced, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and others will no longer be able to dismiss it with the phrase "the user stated the age themselves."

📌 Bitcoin price stalls near $82K as key resistance holds 

🌐 Bitcoin price pulled back after briefly breaking above $82,000 on Sept. 4, as traders took profits following a short squeeze driven by softer Federal Reserve expectations and renewed demand for US spot Bitcoin ETFs. According to data from cryptonews, Bitcoin price traded near $81,150 at the time of writing, having failed to hold an intraday move above the $82,000 psychological level. The pullback left the asset about 1% below its local high but still well above the $80,000 mark reclaimed during the previous session. 

⚠️ The rally accelerated after Bitcoin moved out of a range around $77,000–$79,000. Short sellers were forced to close leveraged positions as the price crossed $80,000, adding automatic buy orders to the market. CoinGlass data cited by market reports showed that the broader crypto market recorded more than $500 million in liquidations during the rally, with short positions accounting for most of the total. Bitcoin shorts reportedly absorbed about $415 million of those losses.

📊 Price action has since slowed near a technically important area. Galaxy Research data shared by analyst Quinten François placed Bitcoin’s 50-week moving average near $81,041, almost level with the current market price. According to François, Bitcoin has not closed a weekly candle above that moving average since November 2025. He said a move through $82,800 would also produce the first higher high of the broader downtrend and bring $90,000 back into consideration.

🌐 Coldcard hacker uses THORChain to swap stolen BTC 

📣 A hacker associated with the third wave of Coldcard wallet thefts began converting stolen Bitcoin into Ether through THORChain on Sept. 3, according to Galaxy Research’s Alex Thorn. The transactions moved approximately 10% of the Bitcoin controlled by that attacker. Roughly 90% remained at its original addresses when he published the update. 

🔖 Researchers traced the swaps through THORChain to a newly identified Ethereum address. Thorn said he shared the address with law enforcement, crypto companies and other organizations monitoring the stolen assets. However, not every transaction succeeded. Thorn said the hacker appeared to be experiencing technical problems while attempting to process the swaps.

🔔 The cause of the refunds was not immediately confirmed. Possible explanations include liquidity limitations, transaction settings or protocol safeguards, but no verified technical assessment had established the reason. The movement represented the first detected onchain transfer from the original addresses associated with the first three attack waves, according to Thorn. Analysts will now monitor whether the resulting ETH moves to centralized exchanges, bridges or privacy services.

Dear Leaders, Partners, and Members of the METATRONICS Community,

Over the past few days, we have observed information about METATRONICS being actively circulated within certain communities and private communications, containing serious allegations against the company and its management.

Until now, we have deliberately chosen not to bring internal disagreements into the public space. We believe that a professional company should address such matters based on facts and documented evidence, rather than through conflicts in group chats or emotional public statements.

However, the situation has now gone beyond the boundaries of a personal dispute.

The information currently being circulated affects the reputation of METATRONICS, raises understandable questions among our leaders and partners, and, in our view, presents a distorted picture of what has actually occurred.

For this reason, we are compelled to publicly clarify the company’s position and provide our community with the other side of the situation.

This concerns an individual who worked with METATRONICS for an extended period of time in the role of Global Ambassador and was entrusted with a significant level of confidence by both the company and the community.

The company provided this individual with financial and organizational support, made payments, and allocated resources to support the development of his organization and those of his generals. All relevant transactions and actions taken by the company are documented.

Today, this individual is making serious allegations against METATRONICS. At the same time, there are several circumstances that we believe our community also has the right to be aware of.

First — financial demands made to the company.

After questions were raised regarding future plans and the Global Ambassador’s failure to meet the agreed KPIs, METATRONICS management received a demand for a payment of $600,000.

At the same time, the company received statements indicating that if this demand was not met, negative information about the project would be circulated.

This form of interaction is unacceptable to us.

METATRONICS does not make payments under pressure and does not make financial decisions in response to reputational threats — regardless of an individual’s status, the size of their organization, or their history of cooperation with the company.

Second — financial relationships within the organization.

We have also received information indicating that certain members of the organization may have been asked to provide personal funds under promises of future compensation, reimbursement, redistribution, or the use of those funds for “development.”

If you have personally encountered such situations, we ask you to provide the company with any supporting materials available to you, including correspondence, amounts, dates, and transaction records.

Each such case will be reviewed individually.

It is important to understand that private financial arrangements entered into between members of the organization without the official approval of METATRONICS do not constitute financial obligations of the company.

Third — the position of METATRONICS regarding further cooperation.

As of now, this individual no longer represents METATRONICS and is not authorized to speak or act on behalf of the company.

Any future statements, promises, or financial arrangements made by this individual do not represent the official position of METATRONICS unless they are separately confirmed by the company through its official channels.

At the same time, we have no intention of turning this situation into a public war.

Every individual has the right to end their cooperation with the company, criticize its decisions, and hold their own opinion.

But there is a fundamental difference between an opinion and specific allegations presented as facts.

When serious claims are made publicly against a company, they should be supported by evidence.
